paras: The shooting at Samuel R. Hurst was an attack at Laredo, Texas, in late summer 1881 in which unidentified assailants fired three or four times at Hurst, a Black man recently appointed inspector, or river guard, on the Rio Grande. He was not reported hurt, and the papers that carried the story tied the attack to his color.

According to the San Antonio Express, Hurst was "a mulatto" from New Orleans who had recently taken up the duties of inspector, or river guard, at Laredo. The Express wrote that the people around Laredo did not seem to like the idea of "a colored inspector" being appointed to watch them, and that they were "rebellious."

A man who had just come up from Laredo told the Express that Hurst had been shot at three or four times "the other night" and had "barely escaped being killed." A shorter brief described the guard as having been "several times" fired upon and said it was believed that Mexicans had done it, "on account of his color." Neither report named a shooter, gave the exact date or place of the attack, or mentioned any wound.
No report of an arrest, investigation or official response appears in the coverage.

The earliest surviving report is a reprint of the Express item in the Washington Evening Critic on 3 September 1881, headed "Call Out the Troops," which presented the shooting as local resistance to a Black officer. Within a week a one-sentence version, without Hurst's name, ran in the crime columns of the River Falls Journal and the Iowa County Democrat in Wisconsin, set among murders, embezzlements and arrests. That brief called him "a negro river guard" and named his color as the motive, while the Express version spoke of "a mulatto" and "a colored inspector."
Apart from the Express credit in the Washington reprint, no Texas paper's report of the shooting appears in the coverage.

The two versions differ on the attackers and the number of attacks: the brief speaks of several attacks believed to be by Mexicans, while the Express account names no shooter and describes three or four shots on a single night.

reader.title: Shooting at Samuel R. Hurst
bases: Unidentified assailants fired on a Black customs inspector at Laredo three or four times one night, without reported injury, amid local hostility to his appointment (A2, A3).

Two differently worded reports (A2, A3) agree on the core event, but A2 is credited to the San Antonio Express and A3 is an uncredited crime brief that likely condenses the same Texas report, so they cannot be shown to be independent; A4 reprints A3.

framing.detail: The Evening Critic reprinted the Express item under "Call Out the Troops," calling the local people "rebellious" over a "colored inspector" without comment on the shooting itself.
Wisconsin weeklies ran an identical one-sentence brief in a crime column, attributing the shooting to Mexicans "on account of his color."
